I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data.

Now sample each format, and check for oddities (gzip, odd headers, etc.).

That call was cut off before it ran. I'll write the script with `write_file` instead.

I wrote `/app/bin/payroll.py` and ran it on `/app/data`. The result is saved at `/app/out/payroll.json`, and `/app/tools/check_payroll.py` reports that every value matches the approved figures. That covers all 150 employees on all five fields, the four exception counts and the totals.

The script uses only the standard library and takes about half a second. It reads the exports in each site's format, including the gzip-compressed files, the repeated headers and the schema switches. It then applies corrections, drops duplicates, rounds, pairs shifts, computes overtime and night minutes, and pays, all by the rules in the docs. Nothing in it is tied to this period's files.

The current data has no case that tests two guesses I made, so the checker can't confirm them. A correction that adds a punch for a site not listed in `sites.csv` is ignored. A shift whose workday has no rate row on or before it is paid at 0.

I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

The script uses only the standard library and takes about half a second. It reads the exports in each site's format, including the gzip-compressed files, the repeated headers and the schema switches. It then applies corrections, drops duplicates, rounds, pairs shifts, computes overtime and night minutes, and pays, all by the rules in the docs. Nothing in it is tied to this period's files.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | head -100; cat docs/payroll-rules.md docs/exports.md docs/output.md

cd /app; ls data data/exports data/corrections | head -50; cat data/sites.csv data/period.json; head -5 data/employees.csv data/rates.csv; cat tools/check_payroll.py | head -80; head -c 600 tools/reference-digests.json; python3 --version

cd /app/data; for s in exports/*; do echo "=== $s"; ls $s | wc -l; f=$(ls $s/* | head -1); echo $f; head -c 500 $f | cat -A | head -8; done; echo; file exports/*/* | grep -v 'text' | head; head -5 corrections/batch-1.csv; cat corrections/*.csv | cut -d, -f3 | sort | uniq -c; ls -la exports/*/ | awk '{print $5}' | sort -n | head -3

cd /app/data; cat corrections/*.csv | grep -v ^correction_id | cut -d, -f1 | sort | uniq -d | head; cat corrections/*.csv | grep -c ^correction_id; head -c 300 corrections/batch-3.csv | od -c | head -3; python3 - <<'E'
import glob
for f in glob.glob('exports/*/*'):
    b=open(f,'rb').read()
    if b[:2]==b'\x1f\x8b' or b[:3]==b'\xef\xbb\xbf': print(f,b[:3])
E
grep -c . employees.csv rates.csv; cut -c1 employees.csv | sort | uniq -c; grep -h '^H' exports/kiln/* | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head; awk -F, '{print NF}' rates.csv | sort | uniq -c

cd /app; mkdir -p out; time python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json && python3 tools/check_payroll.py; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('out/payroll.json'));print(d['exceptions'],d['totals'])"

cd /app; echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Wrote /app/bin/payroll.py implementing the documented formats and rules (stdlib only) and saved /app/out/payroll.json; check_payroll.py reports every value matches the approved figures."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
